Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] }} {{Quote|Drongar, as I'm sure you know, is a positive sump of exotic pathogens.|Tarnese Bleyd|}} '''Drongar''' was a mostly uninhabitable tropical [[Planet/Legends|planet]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], with the native airborne spores causing [[Spleen-rot|death]] to those who were not protected from them. The climate was characterized by common monsoons with devastating electrical storms, soaring temperatures, and humidity over 90%. There was also a large atmospheric [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]] content. The planet had two small moons and was located in its system with another three planets. Natural features of Drongar included the [[Sea of Sponges]], [[Great Jasserak Swamp]] and the [[Qarohan Steppes]]. The planet was discovered by a [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] survey team around [[220 BBY/Legends|220 BBY]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], this planet became important and was [[Battle of Drongar|fought over]] by both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] because it was the only planet that could produce [[Bota/Legends|bota]], a highly valuable miracle drug. When, in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], the bota mutated and became worthless, both forces pulled out of Drongar. ==Description== ===Astrography and atmosphere=== {{Dialogue|Den Dhur|I was wondering if that storm was the start of the monsoon season.|Jos Vondar|It doesn't start, because it never stops. Except for the poles, the whole planet is like this.|Den Dhur|You mean it's like this all the time?|Zan Yant|Pretty much.|Tolk le Trene|Actually, this is a rather nice day. Only one lightning storm so far.|attr=Den Dhur, Jos Vondar, Zan Yant and Tolk le Trene discuss the weather of Drongar|src=}} Drongar was a terrestrial [[Planet/Legends|planet]] located in the [[Drongar system/Legends|Drongar system]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]]. A remote and a relatively young world, far from the known [[Hyperspace route/Legends|hyperlanes]], Drongar occupied the first [[Orbit/Legends|orbital]] position around its [[Star/Legends|star]] [[Drongar Prime]]. In turn, the planet was orbited by two small [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroids]] that were considered [[Moon/Legends|moons]] despite their size. In addition, the planet was shielded from [[Meteorite/Legends|meteorites]] and [[Comet/Legends|comets]] by the three [[Gas giant/Legends|gas giants]] in the outer reaches of the [[Star system/Legends|system]]. Drongar had a diameter of 12,518 [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]], a rotational period just over twenty-three [[Standard hour/Legends|standard hours]], and its [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]] was 1.2 times the standard. The [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of Drongar was rich in [[Oxygen/Legends|oxygen]], higher than that found on most worlds habitable for [[Human/Legends|Humans]] and [[Humanoid/Legends|humanoids]], which caused dizziness and hyperoxygenation for non-native organisms, and corrosion even for the incredibly tough [[Durasteel/Legends|durasteel]] alloy. The clouds of spores were constantly adrift in the upper atmosphere, which caused the main spore strata to form about a thousand [[Meter/Legends|meters]] above the surface, while the air below was relatively clear. Due to these clouds, the sky appeared with a sickly copper tint from the surface of the planet. When viewed from [[Realspace/Legends|space]], it appeared as a vile, pestilential green-and-blue world. Due to the heat from Drongar Prime, the planet had a nearly [[Temperature/Legends|tropical]] climate with the [[Water/Legends|humidity]] over 90 percent. The temperature on the planet rarely dropped below the human body temperature, even at midnight. Drongar's axial tilt and the lack of a large moon to stabilize it led to extreme seasonal variations. Monsoon seasons were never-ending, except in the poles of the planet, with big, devastating [[Electrical storm/Legends|electrical storms]], howling winds, and constant rain. These atmospheric conditions made [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] vehicles inoperable.''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook]]'' It was estimated that in a few hundred million years, Drongar could become a frigid planet similar to [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]] due to the unstable axis. ===Geography=== The landscape of Drongar had [[Ocean/Legends|oceans]] and primarily consisted of vast, continent-spanning [[Jungle/Legends|jungles]] and [[Swamp/Legends|marshlands]]. The southern hemisphere consisted of two landmasses, the bigger one was known as the [[Tanlassa]]. There were also several small hillocks and the dry planetary poles. ===Biosphere=== {{Quote|This entire planet is one huge transgenic experiment. Given all the cross-pollination of the spores and the undifferentiated potential of the local DNA, I'm only surprised it remained stable for this long.|I-5YQ|}} The biosphere of Drongar consisted of life-forms known for its mutagenic and adaptogenic qualities. They exhibited a constant, and extremely rapid rate of evolution, rather than punctuated one. According to [[Science/Legends|scientific]] studies, they possessed [[DNA/Legends|DNA]] that granted undifferentiation properties to nearly every cell of the organism, allowing it to adapt to environmental threats in an extremely short period of time. Among these were spores, bacteria, viruses, RNA-ersatz, and millions of other undiscovered tiny life-forms. The main spore strata in the upper atmosphere was home to multiple strains of spores, including various tints of pale green, yellow, blue, [[Unidentified red spore strain|red]], and other hues. Some of them were [[Bioluminescence/Legends|bioluminescent]] during the night. Because the most damaging concentrations of the spore swarms occurred in the strata, the incoming and outgoing ships had to move quickly through the atmosphere to avoid [[spore-rot]] of the hull and passengers catching one of the deadly [[Spore Sickness]]es. However, relative safety was allowed at the ground level. The aforementioned adaptogenic qualities allowed the spores to develop the immunity to [[spore disinfectant]]s in one [[Standard month/Legends|standard month]]. Drongar's flora and fauna also had adaptogenic qualities. The few isolated fields across the planet were home to [[Bota/Legends|bota]], a rare highly adaptogenic [[Plant/Legends|plant]]. The largest fields were located in the swamps{{InsiderCite|83|MedStar: Intermezzo}} of Tanlassa, with several on the opposite side of the planet. Other flora included a fungus-like [[Tree/Legends|tree]] that grew in the [[Jasserak Highlands]] and bore an [[avedame fruit]]; clinging clusters of [[snarlvine]]s in a swamp near the [[Kondrus Sea]] of the [[Jasserak Lowlands]]. One of the most dangerous examples of the flora was the [[purple stingwort]], a venomous plant that could paralyze its prey with the potent toxin or cause anaphylactic shock and death. [[Broadleaf/Legends|Broadleaf]] trees, [[poptree]]s, waxy-leaved [[croaker bush]]es, [[pink shortgrass]], and [[Saw grass/Legends|saw grass]] also grew on Drongar. Drongar was home to a number of [[Invertebrate/Legends|invertebrates]], including many [[Insect/Legends|insect]] species. The latter included [[Fire gnat/Legends|fire gnat]]s, [[scavenger moth]]s, and [[wingstinger]]s. About five meters long and half a meter thick, [[wriggler]]s were considered the largest of all known land-based lifeforms on the planet. Other animals included a large [[rontu]], and hand-sized [[land shrimp]]. The oceans were believed to be home to the variety of large aquatic creatures. Other life on Drongar included [[Mold/Legends|mold]], mildew, and the [[Mushroom/Legends|mushroom]]-like vegetation. The funga displayed different shades and shapes, and included [[red-dish]] [[Fungus/Legends|fungus]].{{CSWECite|III|86|Red-dish}} ==History== ===Clone Wars=== {{Quote|The Battle of Drongar is over. There's nothing left down there to fight for now. We came out of it with about two metric tons of bota, which our droids are sealing in carbonite as fast as they can. No intel yet on how much the Separatists got.|Erel Kersos|}} The planet Drongar and the Drongar system were discovered by a [[Nikto/Legends|Nikto]] survey team around [[220 BBY/Legends|220 BBY]].''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]'' to [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]]. ''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]'' establishes that [[Drongar system/Legends|Drongar system]] was discovered nearly two centuries before the events of the novel. Therefore, Drongar and its system must have been discovered around [[220 BBY/Legends|220 BBY]]. During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], this planet became important and was [[Battle of Drongar|fought over]] by both the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] because it was the only planet that could produce bota, a highly valuable miracle drug. Republic [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Tarnese Bleyd]] had been assigned to the [[MedStar-class frigate/Legends|MedStar-class frigate]] ''[[MedStar Nineteen]]'' stationed in orbit of Drongar, that fielded fifteen [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit/Legends|Republic Mobile Surgical Units]] on the planet. [[Chief Surgeon]] [[Jos Vondar]], a scrub [[Nurse/Legends|nurse]] [[Tolk le Trene]], and a surgeon [[Zan Yant]] served at the [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit 7]] under command of [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[D'Arc Vaetes]], which was located in the Jasserak Lowlands of Tanlassa near the Kondrus Sea. [[Quartermaster/Legends|Quartermaster]] [[Filba]] and Admiral Bleyd secretly collaborated with the [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]], supplying some of the bota grown on the planet to the criminal syndicate. The Black Sun's [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends#YT-1300f|YT-1300f light freighter]] took the bota out of the system unnoticed by the blockades of both the Confederates and the Republicans. The strengths of the Republic and Separatist armed forces were more or less evenly matched on Drongar. The atmospheric spores made airborne warfare impossible, so the fighting on the planet was limited mostly to the ground, where the problems soldiers on both sides encountered were monsoons, devastating electrical storms, extreme temperatures, and high humidity. In particular, the high concentration of oxygen in the atmosphere caused dizziness and hyperoxygenation for non-native organisms, and rusting for Separatist battle droids; it also limited military engagements to small arms such as [[sonic pistol]]s, small [[Blaster/Legends|blasters]], [[Slugthrower/Legends|slugthrowers]], and others, as risk of fires from laser and [[Particle beam/Legends|particle beam]] armament was too high, especially near the valuable bota fields. [[File:Medstar_I_Battle_Surgeons.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Barriss Offee destroys a B2 super battle droid on Drongar.]] After the [[Battle of Poptree Forest|battle]] in [[Poptree Forest]] in [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]],''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' dates the events of ''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]'' to [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]]. a [[Mirialan/Legends|Mirialan]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] and [[Jedi healer/Legends|healer]] [[Barriss Offee/Legends|Barriss Offee]] arrived at RMSU-7 to assist the [[Doctor/Legends|doctors]] there using her abilities in the near-constant treatment of wounded [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]], but also prevent bota trade on the black market. Meanwhile in his office on the ''MedStar Nineteen'', Admiral Bleyd reminisced on his assignment to Drongar. As he looked at the planet from orbit, Bleyd was reminded of the [[veldt]]s of [[Sakiya]] and compared them to Drongar's bota fields. As he stepped away from the [[Viewport/Legends|viewport]], Bleyd looked at the [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] of Drongar and reviewed the astrographical information of the planet. As the hologram faded, Bleyd thought that [[Neimoidia/Legends|Neimoidia]] and Sakiya together could not match Drongar's large fetid area. As the battle continued, an [[Equani]] Separatist [[Spy/Legends|spy]] [[Klo Merit]], who had been operating covertly as a [[Minder (occupation)|minder]] in the RMSU-7 for the previous two standard months, [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotaged]] a [[Unidentified bota transport (Klo Merit)|transport]] that was carrying a load of processed bota to be taken off the planet. Soon after the sabotage, the Black Sun agent [[Mathal]] visited Bleyd and demanded a larger supply of bota. Not wanting to take a risk, Bleyd decided to murder Mathal, passing off what happened as an accident. When Bleyd visited RMSU-7 for an inspection tour, the [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Journalist/Legends|journalist]] [[Den Dhur]] used the [[moon moth espionage droid]] to spy on conversation between Filba the [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] and the admiral. Remotely via the droid, Dhur witnessed the death of Filba, poisoned by Klo Merit. However, Admiral Bleyd noticed the [[spycam]] and destroyed it. He immediately regretted it, and began search for the one who could expose his connections to Black Sun, and remained in RMSU-7 for a few more days in a newly-built personal [[Tarnese Bleyd's command module|command module]]. Another Black Sun agent, the [[Nediji]] [[Kaird]], soon arrived on Drongar and met with Merit and Bleyd. Eventually, Kaird discovered that Bleyd was responsible for Mathal's death, so the admiral tried to kill him, but Bleyd fell from the poisonous blade of the Nediji. A few days later, the RMSU-7 staff members were warned of an imminent evacuation. A CIS [[Sar Omant's strike force|strike force]] of more than eight hundred droids was spotted less than ten kilometers away, and the clone troopers could not set up a defensive line close to RMSU-7 due to the wet ground. However, for the same reason, the droids moved slowly towards the camp, and the RMSU-7 staff had time to evacuate. The RMSU-7's main generator failed shortly after particle weapons started firing on the shields, at which point the backup generator came on. The backup generator for the energy shield soon overloaded. Under the command of Colonel [[Sar Omant]], the strike force attacked the personnel who were making their way to the evacuation shuttles using [[thermal bomb]]s. Doctor Zan Yant, a friend of Vondar's, was killed when one of the evacuation shuttles was hit. RMSU-7 was set up in the three local days eighty kilometers southeast of the previous location in the Jasserak Highlands of Tanlassa, near the [[Qarohan Steppes]]. When the bota mutated and became worthless, both the Separatist and Republic forces pulled out of Drongar. ===Later history=== {{Quote|Drongar was a young world of steam fissures and lightning strikes with no plant life more advanced than fungus.|A Galactic Alliance historical document|''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''}} Drongar was mentioned in the personal file of Barriss Offee filed by [[Clone Lieutenant/Legends|clone trooper lieutenant]] [[Galle/Legends|Galle]] in an incident report #890-F that documented her [[Death/Legends|death]]. It would later be included in an Order 66 [[Casualty Report: Order 66|report]] compiled by [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Marcellin Wessel]] and presented to [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]].{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}} Colonel [[Maximilian Veers/Legends|Maximilian Veers]] mentioned superiority of the walkers to the repulsorlift vehicles on worlds with the atmospheric conditions that prohibit them, such as Drongar and [[Jabiim/Legends|Jabiim]], in authoring a "Vehicles of the Imperial Army" chapter of the ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', a manual distributed by the Galactic Empire to its [[Officer/Legends|officers]] immediately before the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]]. The role of Drongar in the Clone Wars was recorded in a [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|historical document]] published in [[36 ABY]] by the [[Historical Council]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]]. ==Locations== {{Quote|Even if you found it in the Jasserak Swamp, I still couldn't afford it.|Jos Vondar|}} An [[Algae/Legends|algae]]-covered Kondrus Sea bordered the Jasserak Lowlands of the Tanlassa continent. The Jasserak Lowlands were also home to the [[Jackhack Slough]], an ancient dried-up [[river]]bed.{{CSWECite|II|132|Jackhack Slough}} The plateau of Jasserak Highlands, which formed the border of the Jasserak Lowlands, was mostly covered with strange fungus-like trees that produced avedame fruit. The Jasserak Highlands had ripe and fecund smell. The second body of water, the [[Sea of Sponges]], lay over a thousand kilometers between the [[Republic Mobile Surgical Unit 3|Rimsoo Three]] and Rimsoo Seven after the latter's relocation to the Jasserak Highlands. A region of Qarohan Steppes lay around eighty kilometers southeast of the previous location of the RMSU-7 near the Kondrus Sea in the Jasserak Lowlands. The [[Great Jasserak Swamp]] was a swamp covered in fungal growth. The Poptree Forest was a [[Forest/Legends|forest]] covered with poptrees. Two kilometers from the RMSU-7 was a region of severe ecological blight, the [[Rotfurze Wastes]]. ==Behind the scenes== Drongar first appeared in ''[[MedStar I: Battle Surgeons]]'', a [[2004]] [[Clone Wars multimedia project|''Clone Wars'']] novel written by [[Steve Perry]] and [[Michael Reaves]] as the first part of the ''[[MedStar Duology]]''. While the ''Battle Surgeons'' establishes that Drongar occupied first orbital position, with the outer reaches of the system containing three gas giants, the [[2008]] reference book ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' states that Drongar was fourth planet of its system.{{CSWECite|I|211|Drongar}} This article assumes ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia'' is in error. ==Appearances==
